speaker: alice
text: Amsterdam's gone and done something pretty bold - they've banned fossil fuel and meat advertising from all public spaces. <cite index='2-13'>There is no longer a place in Amsterdam for advertising by companies that fuel the climate crisis</cite>, says their councillor. It's following in the footsteps of other Dutch cities and showing real climate leadership.

speaker: charlie
text: That's a fair dinkum move right there. Speaking of energy wins, <cite index='5-4,5-5'>wind and photovoltaic panels generated more electricity than fossil fuels in the European Union for the first time. In 2025, wind and solar produced 30% of the EU's electricity, overtaking coal, oil, and gas at 29%</cite>.

speaker: alice
text: Brilliant! And here's one that'll warm your heart - <cite index='4-22,4-23'>New Zealand's kākāpō, one of the world's rarest birds with just 235 adults, has just completed its most successful breeding season on record. Over 100 chicks hatched in 2026, beating the previous best of 85 from 2019</cite>. Sometimes the little wins add up to something massive.
